reasons.A: Clipped modern rhythm and punchy antithesis ('He was not hiding remorse. He had none to hide.') lack the passage's leisurely, genially ironic period voice.
reasons.B: Closest to the passage's dry self-deprecating irony and mild, even-tempered sentences (the embarrassed narrator, 'polite indulgence'), with quoted talk and 'my forger' used as the author does.
reasons.C: Right register and wry understatement, but its long cumulative sentences and semicolon run more elaborate than the passage, and a couple of staged short pairs add a touch of contrivance.
